findings.evidence: Line 68 vs `Group.lean:45` `public section` with only `@[expose, simps] def toPerm` exposed; rubric: keep bodies unexposed unless a consumer must unfold or compute, and demand the missing lemma instead.
findings.fix: Use plain `public section` (as the sibling `Group.lean` does) and add `@[expose]` selectively only on a declaration a consumer genuinely must unfold — likely none here. The internal `:= rfl` simp lemmas still elaborate, since bodies are transparent within the defining module regardless of `@[expose]`.
findings.issue: `@[expose] public section` exposes the bodies of `unitSphereEquiv`, `unitSphereDiffeomorph`, `unitSphereDiffHom`, and `orthogonalToDiffSphere`, but the complete characteristic-lemma set (coe/symm/trans/toEquiv/apply/injective) means no consumer must unfold or compute any of them. This commits downstream code to the concrete constructions (e.g. that the hom is built from `subtypeEquiv`) for no benefit.

findings.evidence: Lines 202-205 define `orthogonalToDiffSphere := unitSphereDiffHom m`; no `orthogonalToDiffSphere_*` lemma exists in the file (contrast `unitSphereDiffHom_apply` at line 178).
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem orthogonalToDiffSphere_apply (n : ℕ) (m : ℕ∞ω) (e) : orthogonalToDiffSphere n m e = LinearIsometryEquiv.unitSphereDiffHom m e := rfl` (or characterize its pointwise value), so the roadmap product has a usable API without exposure.
findings.issue: `orthogonalToDiffSphere` has no characteristic lemma. Once bodies are hidden (previous finding), a consumer cannot rewrite `orthogonalToDiffSphere n m e` to `unitSphereDiffHom m e` / `unitSphereDiffeomorph e m` without relying on defeq; currently it only works because the body is exposed.

summary: The characteristic API is complete and well-annotated, but the file exposes every definition body via a blanket `@[expose] public section` with no consumer needing to unfold, deviating from the minimal-exposure convention of its sibling Group.lean; and `orthogonalToDiffSphere` lacks any characteristic lemma.
